notes.title: Frontend Architecture Overview
notes.content:
TechFlow Frontend Architecture — Documentation

Stack:
- Framework: Next.js 14 (App Router)
- UI Library: React 19
- Styling: TailwindCSS + custom design tokens
- State Management: Zustand (lightweight, no Redux bloat)
- Data Fetching: TanStack Query (React Query v5)
- Forms: React Hook Form + Zod validation
- Animation: Framer Motion
- Testing: Vitest + React Testing Library + Playwright (E2E)

Project Structure:
```
app/
  (auth)/         # Authentication pages
  (dashboard)/    # Main app pages
  api/            # API routes
components/
  ui/             # Design system primitives (Button, Input, etc.)
  features/       # Feature-specific components
  layouts/        # Page layouts and shells
lib/
  hooks/          # Custom React hooks
  utils/          # Utility functions
  api/            # API client and types
```

Key Patterns:
- Server Components by default (data fetching at the server)
- Client Components only when needed (interactivity, state)
- Composition over inheritance
- Co-located tests (component.test.tsx next to component.tsx)
- Design tokens as CSS custom properties (not JS runtime)

Performance Budget:
- First Contentful Paint: <1.5s
- Largest Contentful Paint: <2.5s
- Cumulative Layout Shift: <0.1
- Total bundle size: <200KB (gzipped)

Maintainer: Lisa Nakamura

notes.title: Accessibility Audit Findings — WCAG 2.1 AA
notes.content:
TechFlow Accessibility Audit — WCAG 2.1 Level AA
Audit Date: February 3-7, 2026
Auditor: Lisa Nakamura

Methodology:
- Manual testing with screen reader (VoiceOver on macOS)
- Automated scanning (axe-core via Playwright)
- Keyboard-only navigation test
- Color contrast analysis (contrast-checker.com)

Total Issues Found: 23
- Critical (P1): 4
- Major (P2): 8
- Minor (P3): 11

Critical Issues (P1):
1. Document editor: Missing ARIA labels on toolbar buttons
   - Impact: Screen reader users cannot identify formatting tools
   - Fix: Add aria-label to all toolbar IconButton components

2. Modal dialogs: Focus not trapped inside modal
   - Impact: Keyboard users can tab behind the modal
   - Fix: Implement focus trap using FocusTrap component

3. Color-only status indicators: Red/green dots for online/offline
   - Impact: Color-blind users cannot distinguish status
   - Fix: Add text label or icon alongside color indicator

4. Form errors: No programmatic association between error and input
   - Impact: Screen readers don't announce errors
   - Fix: Add aria-describedby linking input to error message

Major Issues (P2):
5. Insufficient color contrast on secondary buttons (3.8:1, need 4.5:1)
6. Images missing alt text in user-uploaded content
7. Skip navigation link missing
8. Heading hierarchy broken (h1 → h3, skipping h2)
9. Dropdown menus not keyboard accessible
10. Toast notifications not announced to screen readers
11. Table data missing header associations
12. Auto-playing animation with no pause control

Remediation Plan:
- P1 issues: Fixed in Sprint 22-23 (DONE)
- P2 issues: Sprint 24-25 (IN PROGRESS)
- P3 issues: Ongoing (1-2 per sprint)

Goal: Full WCAG 2.1 AA compliance by end of Q1 2026.

notes.title: Performance Optimization Notes
notes.content:
Frontend Performance Optimization — Findings & Actions

Date: February 20, 2026
Tools: Lighthouse, Chrome DevTools, WebPageTest

Baseline Metrics (Before):
- LCP: 3.2s (poor)
- FID: 120ms (needs improvement)
- CLS: 0.15 (poor)
- TTI: 4.1s (poor)
- Bundle size: 285KB gzipped

Optimizations Implemented:

1. Code Splitting (Bundle reduction: -60KB)
- Dynamic imports for heavy components (editor, chart library)
- Route-based splitting (each page loads only its code)
- Moved moment.js → date-fns (saved 40KB)

2. Image Optimization (-0.8s LCP)
- Next.js Image component with priority for above-fold
- WebP format with AVIF fallback
- Lazy loading for below-fold images
- Blur placeholder for perceived performance

3. Layout Shift Prevention (-0.12 CLS)
- Explicit width/height on all media elements
- Font display: swap with size-adjust
- Skeleton loaders matching final layout dimensions

4. JavaScript Optimization (-80ms FID)
- Defer non-critical scripts
- Web Workers for heavy computation (markdown parsing)
- Virtualized lists for large datasets (react-window)

Results (After):
- LCP: 1.8s (good ✓)
- FID: 45ms (good ✓)
- CLS: 0.03 (good ✓)
- TTI: 2.4s (good ✓)
- Bundle size: 195KB gzipped (good ✓)

Ongoing Monitoring:
- Lighthouse CI in GitHub Actions (fail if score <90)
- Real User Monitoring via Datadog RUM
- Bundle size check in PR (warn if >5KB increase)

notes.title: React 19 Migration Notes
notes.content:
React 19 Migration — Technical Notes

Migration completed: Sprint 23 (February 28, 2026)
PR: #487 (120 files changed)

Breaking Changes Addressed:

1. useEffect cleanup timing changed
- React 19: Cleanup runs synchronously during unmount
- Impact: 3 components had race conditions with async cleanup
- Fix: Added AbortController pattern for async effects

2. Ref callback changes
- React 19: Ref callbacks can return a cleanup function
- Impact: Refactored 5 components using ref callbacks for DOM measurement
- Benefit: Cleaner pattern than useEffect + ref

3. Context provider simplification
- React 19: <Context> instead of <Context.Provider>
- Impact: Updated all 12 context providers
- Note: Old pattern still works but emits deprecation warning

4. use() hook
- New: Can read context and promises directly in render
- Opportunity: Simplify some data-fetching patterns in future
- Not adopted yet: Waiting for patterns to stabilize

5. Server Components improvements
- React 19: Better async component support
- Impact: Simplified 8 server components (removed Suspense wrappers for simple async)

Hydration Warnings (Remaining):
- 2 warnings related to date formatting (locale mismatch server/client)
- Non-blocking, but should fix (Mike aware)

Performance Impact:
- Bundle size: Neutral (React 19 is slightly smaller)
- Runtime: ~5% improvement in concurrent rendering benchmarks
- No regressions detected in Lighthouse CI

Lesson: Always do major framework upgrades in a dedicated sprint with full test coverage. The 120-file PR was intimidating but all tests passed.

notes.title: Career Ladder Research — Industry Comparison
notes.content:
Career Ladder Research — February 2026

Question: Is TechFlow L3 (Senior) = industry L3 (Senior)?

TechFlow Ladder (from HR doc):
- L1: Junior (intern/new grad) — Jake
- L2: Engineer — Tom
- L3: Senior — Lisa, Mike (soon Staff)
- L4: Staff — Mike (April)
- L5: Principal (future)

Industry Comparison:
- Google: L5 = Senior (equivalent to TechFlow L3)
- Meta: E5 = Senior (equivalent)
- Stripe: L3 = Senior (same numbering!)
- Netflix: Senior (flat hierarchy, all 'Senior')

Comp Comparison (SF, Senior FE, 2026):
- TechFlow L3: $145K base + 0.6% equity + 15% bonus = ~$167K cash + equity
- Google L5: $175K base + $60K RSU + 15% bonus = ~$261K total
- Meta E5: $170K base + $70K RSU + 15% bonus = ~$266K total
- Stripe L3: $180K base + $50K RSU + 10% bonus = ~$248K total
- Startup (Series A, typical): $155-170K + 0.3-0.8% equity + 10-15% bonus

Insight:
- I'm ~$15-30K below market for a startup at my level.
- The gap to Big Tech is larger (~$80-100K/year in cash), but equity is the bet.
- Alex's proposed adjustment ($160K + 0.3%) brings me to competitive-for-startup.
- If I truly wanted max cash, I'd go to FAANG. But I'd lose: impact, ownership, pace.

Decision:
- Stay if retention package comes through as discussed.
- Set a calendar reminder for Q3 to reassess. If Series B happens, reassess equity value.
- Continue politely responding to recruiters to maintain optionality.

notes.title: Accessibility Best Practices Guide
notes.content:
TechFlow — Accessibility Best Practices Guide
(Author: Lisa Nakamura)

For the whole team — not just frontend engineers.

1. Semantic HTML First
- Use <button> for actions, <a> for navigation
- Use heading hierarchy (h1 → h2 → h3, never skip)
- Use <nav>, <main>, <aside>, <footer> landmarks
- Use <ul>/<ol> for lists (screen readers announce count)

2. ARIA When Needed (Not as First Resort)
- aria-label: When visible text isn't descriptive enough
- aria-describedby: For supplementary help text
- aria-expanded: For collapsible sections
- aria-live: For dynamic content updates (toasts, counters)
- Rule: If you can use semantic HTML instead of ARIA, do that.

3. Keyboard Navigation
- All interactive elements must be focusable (tabindex if needed)
- Visible focus indicator (never `outline: none` without alternative)
- Logical tab order (follows visual reading order)
- Escape key closes modals/popovers
- Enter/Space activates buttons

4. Color & Contrast
- Minimum contrast: 4.5:1 for normal text, 3:1 for large text
- Never use color alone to convey information
- Test with Chrome DevTools color vision simulator

5. Images & Media
- All images need alt text (or alt='' for decorative)
- Videos need captions
- Audio content needs transcript

6. Testing Checklist:
☐ Tab through the entire page — can you reach everything?
☐ Use VoiceOver/NVDA — is the experience coherent?
☐ Run axe-core (built into our CI)
☐ Zoom to 200% — does layout hold?
☐ Use with high contrast mode

Resources:
- WCAG 2.1 Quick Reference: w3.org/WAI/WCAG21/quickref/
- axe-core browser extension: deque.com/axe/
- Internal: #accessibility Slack channel (Lisa monitors)

notes.title: Frontend Testing Strategy
notes.content:
Frontend Testing Strategy — TechFlow

Testing Pyramid:
- Unit Tests (70%): Vitest + React Testing Library
- Integration Tests (20%): Component compositions, page-level tests
- E2E Tests (10%): Playwright (critical user journeys only)

Unit Testing Guidelines:
- Test behavior, not implementation
- Query by role/label (accessible queries) — never by test ID unless necessary
- One assertion per test (or one logical behavior)
- Mock: API calls (msw), external libraries. Never mock React internals.

E2E Tests (Playwright):
- Critical journeys only (expensive to maintain):
  1. Sign up → create first document → write content → save
  2. Login → search for document → open → edit → collaborate
  3. Settings → update profile → verify persistence
  4. Share document → recipient can view → access control works

Coverage Targets:
- Component library: 95% (these are foundational)
- Feature components: 80%
- Utility functions: 90%
- E2E: All critical paths have at least 1 test

CI Integration:
- Unit + Integration: Run on every PR (must pass to merge)
- E2E: Run on merge to main (before deploy to staging)
- Lighthouse CI: Run on every PR (score must stay >90)

Current Coverage: 82% (up from 65% in Q4 2025)
Target: 88% by end of Q1 2026
